verdict.rationale: Pomelo documents a first-party transaction simulator that runs entirely in its Stage environment against real cards and a configured authorization endpoint, so developers can exercise their auth logic before production. However, the evidence never lists which lifecycle events the simulator covers. Reversals and refunds are documented only as production adjustment types, not as simulatable cases. Missing for 10: explicit simulator coverage of authorizations, clearings, reversals, refunds and declines; self-serve sandbox access (it is provisioned through the integration team); independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can simulate the whole transaction lifecycle in the sandbox — authorizations, clearings, reversals, refunds, and declines — so my auth logic is tested before a real card ever swipes

citations.quote: Prueba casos de simulación sobre tarjetas reales sin afectar tu ambiente productivo.
Todas las ejecuciones ocurren en nuestro ambiente de Stage.
Recibirás las transacciones de tipo Reversal y Refund a través del endpoint de Ajustes.
